title: RBI KYC Master Direction — Customer Due Diligence & Officially Valid Documents (OVDs)
section: Chapter VI, Part I, Paragraph 16 — Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Procedure in Case of Individuals; Chapter I, Section 3(a)(xiv) — Officially Valid Document
description: Specifies Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) for Customer Due Diligence of individuals and provides for accepted documentation where a name change occurred subsequent to issuance.
text: For undertaking Customer Due Diligence (CDD) of individual customers, Regulated Entities (REs) shall obtain proof of possession of Aadhaar number or any Officially Valid Document (OVD) containing details of identity and address, or equivalent electronic document, along with PAN or Form 60. Officially Valid Documents include Passport, Driving Licence, Proof of possession of Aadhaar number, Voter's Identity Card, NREGA job card, or letter issued by the National Population Register. A document shall be deemed to be an OVD even if there is a change in the name subsequent to its issuance, provided it is supported by a marriage certificate issued by the State Government or a Gazette notification indicating such change of name.
applicability: RBI-regulated entities; customer identification and Customer Due Diligence (CDD) of individual customers

title: RBI KYC Master Direction — Customer Acceptance, Fictitious Names & Identification Authenticity
section: Chapter III, Paragraph 10(a)-(b) & Chapter V, Paragraph 13(c) — Customer Acceptance Policy and Customer Identification Procedure
description: Prohibits accounts in fictitious/benami names, requires non-reliability evaluation of furnished documents, and mandates identification procedures when doubts exist regarding authenticity of customer data.
text: Under the Customer Acceptance Policy and Customer Identification Procedure, Regulated Entities (REs) shall ensure that no account is opened in anonymous or fictitious/benami name, and no account is opened where the RE is unable to apply appropriate Customer Due Diligence (CDD) measures due to non-reliability of documents or information furnished. Further, REs shall undertake customer identification procedures whenever there is a doubt about the authenticity or adequacy of customer identification data obtained. Where PAN is obtained, it shall be verified through the verification facility of the issuing authority. Rejection of onboarding must not be without application of mind, and reasons for rejection shall be duly recorded.
applicability: RBI-regulated entities; customer onboarding, account opening, and customer due diligence

title: RBI Master Direction on Credit Information Reporting — Reporting Standards & Credit Appraisal
section: Chapter II, Section 4 & Chapter III, Section 5 — Membership, Data Quality & Credit Information Usage
description: Mandates Credit Institution membership in all Credit Information Companies (CICs), standard reporting of credit records, and utilization of credit reports for credit appraisal.
text: Under the Reserve Bank of India (Credit Information Reporting) Directions, 2025, all Credit Institutions (CIs) are required to become members of all Credit Information Companies (CICs) registered with the RBI. CIs shall report comprehensive borrower credit records in uniform credit reporting formats, maintain high data quality index standards, and utilize credit information reports for credit appraisal and borrower indebtedness evaluation.
applicability: Credit Institutions (commercial banks, cooperative banks, NBFCs, HFCs, ARCs) and Credit Information Companies (CICs)

title: RBI Guidelines on Fair Practices Code for Lenders — Loan Processing and Reason Communication
section: Guidelines on Fair Practices Code for Lenders, Clause 2(a) — Applications for loans and their processing
description: Mandates clear disclosures on loan applications, timely collection of additional documentation, and written communication of the main reason(s) in the event of loan rejection.
text: Under the Fair Practices Code for Lenders, loan application forms shall be comprehensive and transparent regarding fees and terms. Lenders shall establish a system for acknowledging receipt of loan applications. If additional information or documentation is required from the applicant, the lender shall inform the customer promptly. In the event that a loan application is rejected after consideration, the lender shall convey in writing the main reason or reasons that led to the rejection of the loan application.
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks and All-India Financial Institutions

title: RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending — Direct Account Disbursement & Repayment Flow
section: Annex I, Clause 1.1 — Loan Disbursal, Servicing and Repayment
description: Mandates that all digital loan disbursals and repayments occur directly between the borrower's bank account and the Regulated Entity without third-party pass-through or pool accounts.
text: Regulated Entities (REs) shall ensure that all loan disbursements and repayments are executed strictly and directly between the bank account of the borrower and the RE. Disbursals and repayments shall not pass through any pass-through account or pool account of any third party, including Lending Service Providers (LSPs) or Digital Lending Apps (DLAs), ensuring a direct, auditable fund flow.
applicability: Regulated Entities (Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, NBFCs) engaged in digital lending
